questions.q: What did Jehu’s letter tell the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants to do?
questions.a: It told the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants to select the best and most deserving of their master’s descendants and set him on his father’s throne and then defend him.

questions.q: Why did the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants not make any man king?
questions.a: They did not make any man king because they realized that not even the two kings could stand before Jehu.

questions.q: What did the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants do to the king’s sons?
questions.a: They took the king’s sons and killed them, seventy persons, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.

questions.q: Why did Jehu say that no part of Yahweh’s word, the word that he spoke concerning the family of Ahab, would fall to the ground?
questions.a: Jehu said that no part of Yahweh’s word, the word that he spoke concerning the family of Ahab, would fall to the ground, for Yahweh had done what he spoke about through his servant Elijah.

questions.q: How many brothers of Ahaziah did Jehu meet and kill?
questions.a: He met and killed forty-two men.

questions.q: Why did Jehu take Jonadab into the chariot?
questions.a: Jehu took Jonadab into the chariot because Jonadab said his heart was with Jehu, and he gave Jehu his hand.

questions.q: Why did Jehu gather all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests?
questions.a: He gathered them deceitfully, with the intent to kill the worshipers of Baal.

questions.q: To where did the worshipers of Baal come?
questions.a: They came into the temple of Baal.

questions.q: What would happen if any of the worshipers of Baal escaped?
questions.a: If any of the worshipers of Baal escaped, whoever let that man escape, his life would be taken for the life of he who escaped.

questions.q: Into what did the guards and captains make the house of Baal?
questions.a: They made the house of Baal into a latrine.

questions.q: How did Jehu not leave the sins of Jeroboam?
questions.a: Jehu did not leave the sins of Jeroboam because he worshiped the golden calves in Bethel and Dan.

questions.q: Why would Jehu’s descendants sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation?
questions.a: Because Jehu did well in executing what was right in Yahweh’s eyes, and did to the house of Ahab and did all that was in Yahweh’s heart, his descendants would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

questions.q: Where were the other matters concerning Jehu written?
questions.a: The other matters concerning Jehu, and all that he did, and all his power, were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

commentary.text: Ahab's sons and Ahaziah's brethren put to death.
Jehu destroys the worshippers of Baal.

Verses 1–14 In the most awful events, though attended by the basest crimes of man, the truth and justice of God are to be noticed; and he never did nor can command any thing unjust or unreasonable. Jehu destroyed all that remained of the house of Ahab; all who had been partners in his wickedness. When we think upon the sufferings and miseries of mankind, when we look forward to the resurrection and last judgment, and think upon the vast number of the wicked waiting their awful sentence of everlasting fire; when the whole sum of death and misery has been considered, the solemn question occurs, Who slew all these? The answer is, SIN. Shall we then harbour sin in our bosoms, and seek for happiness from that which is the cause of all misery?

Is thine heart right? This is a question we should often put to ourselves. I make a fair profession, have gained a reputation among men, but, is my heart right? Am I sincere with God? Jehonadab owned Jehu in the work, both of revenge and of reformation. An upright heart approves itself to God, and seeks no more than his acceptance; but if we aim at the applause of men, we are upon a false foundation. Whether Jehu looked any further we cannot judge. The law of God was express, that idolaters were to be put to death. Thus idolatry was abolished for the present out of Israel. May we desire that it be rooted out of our hearts.

It is justly questionable whether Jehu acted from a good principle, and whether he did not take some false steps in doing it; yet no services done for God shall go unrewarded. But true conversion is not only from gross sin, but from all sin; not only from false gods, but from false worships. True conversion is not only from wasteful sins, but from gainful sins; not only from sins which hurt our worldly interests, but from those that support and befriend them; in forsaking which is the great trial whether we can deny ourselves and trust God. Jehu showed great care and zeal for rooting out a false religion, but in the true religion he cared not, took no heed to please God and do his duty. Those that are heedless, it is to be feared, are graceless. The people were also careless, therefore it is not strange that in those days the Lord began to cut Israel short. They were short in their duty to God, therefore God cut them short in their extent, wealth, and power.
